basis: The repaired proof is self-contained and valid. For pumping length p=3 it treats every long word s^r q: it pumps a q-symbol when r is not 1 and q is nonempty, pumps the lone initial s when r=1, and pumps two or three s symbols for the remaining pure-prefix cases, so every pumped word stays in L. Intersecting with regular s a* b* c* isolates s{a^n b^n c^n}; deleting s by homomorphism would make the standard non-CFL context-free. Stanford CS103 gives the exact CFL pumping quantifiers, and Wise 1976 confirms the ordinary condition is not sufficient. The unsupported F1/F2 assertions rejected earlier are absent from the current text.

The two fatal defects have been repaired: Choice is explicit and L1 now uses only the cited forward implication. May, Notes on Dedekind Rings section 6, proves directly that for ideals A contained in B in a Dedekind ring, AB inverse is integral and A equals (AB inverse)B; Proposition 6.1 identifies inclusion with reversed prime-exponent inequalities. Applied with A=J and B=I, this is exactly I containing J if and only if I divides J. The current exponent proof matches that result, and the scoped proof contract passes.

Both fatal defects are repaired in the current definition. The single variable-arity encoder E begins with the unary arity header 1^k0, so distinct arities diverge before any tuple payload, while each length-prefixed c(w) block is effectively and uniquely parsed. The total decoder now rejects absent or malformed headers and blocks, noncanonical numerals, invalid machine parameters, incorrect arity, and out-of-range transitions by returning a fixed malformed-code symbol. These checks establish a total effective decoder and unique recovery of every valid coded machine.

Both exact fatal defects are repaired. The definition now imposes lambda(p,s)=empty for every p and lambda(t,q)=empty for every q, matching the stated no-incoming-start and no-outgoing-accept convention. It also quantifies an integer n at least zero in P_K(p,q), consistently indexes the n edges and n factors, restricts precisely the intermediate states r_1 through r_(n-1), and explicitly defines the zero-length case as p=q with empty factorization and word epsilon. The resulting accepted-language definition is well typed and complete.

Both fatal defects are repaired and the present page proves well-definedness directly. It fixes A, b, and the polynomial ring over the field R or C. For an n-by-n matrix, linear dependence of b, Ab, through A^n b supplies a nonzero annihilating polynomial; choosing least degree and dividing by its nonzero leading coefficient gives a monic annihilator. Two distinct monic least-degree annihilators would have a nonzero difference of smaller degree that still annihilates b, a contradiction. The separate b=0 convention correctly gives q=1 and grade zero.

Both fatal defects are repaired, and authoritative definitions agree with the result. The current page first equips S with its slice-chart smooth structure, cites that the inclusion i is a smooth embedding, and only then identifies T_pS with di_p(T_pS). It explicitly defines TM restricted to S and T-star-M restricted to S as fibrewise disjoint unions over the possibly nonopen base S. Peter Hintz, Introduction to Microlocal Analysis, Exercise 5.5, and Richard Melrose, MIT 18.156 notes, define the normal bundle as T_S M / TS and the conormal bundle as the covectors over S annihilating TS, exactly as here.

Both fatal defects are repaired. The definition now requires the universal machine U to have binary input alphabet, so the encoded machine/input pair is a well-typed input. It states universality behaviorally: an output-producing halt of M must be reproduced with the encoded output, and divergence of M must be reproduced by divergence of U. The former invalid equivalence with a partial function on every halting pair has been removed, and the remark explicitly says that a halting configuration with no output word under the strict output convention imposes no condition. Thus there is no longer an undefined output value.

Both fatal defects are repaired. The definition declares k as a natural number satisfying zero at most k at most the ambient rank r before any rank-k or k-frame notation is used. It does not assume that the subset S already carries a vector-bundle structure: condition 1 requires each fibre intersection to be a k-dimensional linear subspace, and condition 2 directly requires an ambient local frame whose first k values span S intersect E_p at every base point in the neighborhood. The explicit spanning equation supplies the intended meaning and removes the prior circular use of a local frame of S.

Both fatal citation defects are repaired. Fact F1 now cites Alfred Aho, Columbia COMS W3261 Lecture 11, whose section 4 explicitly lists whether two given CFGs generate the same language among undecidable problems. Fact L1 accurately restores the repository definition requirement that the grammars are over the same alphabet. Since a normalization-based decision procedure for all such pairs would decide that undecidable equivalence problem, the direct contradiction is valid. The focused proof contract checks this item with zero errors and zero warnings.

Both unsupported-meta-claim defects are repaired by a complete proof. With pumping length three, the page separately handles r=0, r=1, r at least two with nonempty q, and the remaining pure powers s^r; the chosen v has positive pumped length, the local window has length at most three, and every pumping exponent keeps the word in L. Intersecting L with the regular language s a-star b-star c-star yields exactly sK, and deleting s by homomorphism would make K={a^n b^n c^n} context free, contradicting the cited result. Stanford and Columbia course notes verify the standard pumping quantifiers and non-CFL witness, and the focused proof contract passes.

The two escalated branch defects are repaired, and manual source review found and fixed an additional fatal parameter compression. The page now reproduces those parameters rather than reusing one incompatible c. Focused precheck, rendering, content policy, strict proof contract, boundary audit, citation fidelity, and diff checks pass.
